A1.justification: Both PDFs describe STRAP and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendix A.1-A.6. The complete material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original LIBERO simulation experiments, DROID-Kitchen and Franka-Pen-in-Cup robot experiments, ablations, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in the main text and appendices, including quantitative policy performance and scalability measurements.

M1.justification: The segmentation, foundation-model embeddings, S-DTW retrieval, policy architecture, and training loss are retained. Section 4.5 newly documents a backtracking-step constraint, but the PDFs do not establish that the implemented procedure changed.

E1.justification: Both versions use LIBERO-10/90, DROID-Kitchen with and without additional DROID data, and Franka-Pen-in-Cup, including its out-of-distribution evaluation. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 3 retain BC, FT, MT, BehaviorRetrieval, FlowRetrieval, D-S, and D-T. The real-world comparisons and Appendix A.4 diffusion-policy comparisons also retain their respective comparator sets.

E3.justification: Demonstration counts, training budgets, observation settings, randomization, and evaluation metrics are unchanged. Section 5.1 rewords the kitchen dataset description but still specifies 150 demonstrations across three scenes, with 50 per scene.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same representation and retrieval-granularity comparisons, K sensitivity analysis, retrieval-seed analysis, pen-in-cup robustness test, runtime analysis, and qualitative retrieval distributions. No analysis or supporting evidence is added.

E5.justification: The three training/evaluation seeds in Appendix A.1, training/retrieval seed combinations in Table 9, standard-deviation reporting, and timing repetition counts in Appendix A.5 are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical entries, plotted results, and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains 58.1% ± 32.0 for STRAP with DINOv2 and best K on LIBERO-10.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 removes D(0,0)=C(0,0) from the DTW and S-DTW initializations and changes the full-DTW backtracking endpoint from D(0,0) to D(1,1). These partially correct mixed boundary indexing; the recurrence and complexity analysis remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about sub-trajectory retrieval, cross-task data sharing, few-shot policy performance, robustness, and scalability. The claimed contribution and its scope are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.5 adds a specific rationale for constraining S-DTW backtracking: avoiding degenerate matches. Existing interpretations of performance, negative transfer, representation quality, and chunking failures remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.5 newly specifies that S-DTW backtracking step size is limited to [1, 2], supplying a previously unstated implementation constraint. Hardware, training details, software references, and access information are otherwise unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, bibliography, and novelty positioning are unchanged. The added backtracking sentence cites Müller (2021), which was already cited for DTW, without introducing a new work or revising the research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds the ICLR 2025 publication header, adds a second affiliation for Marius Memmel, rephrases the kitchen demonstration count, and makes localized technical edits. Section order and the overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds a running publication header and has small text and equation spacing changes around the edited passages. Figures and tables retain their content, numbering, structure, and placement, including in the appendices.

improvement.justification: The boundary-index corrections in Section 3.1 and explicit backtracking constraint in Section 4.5 modestly improve mathematical clarity and reproducibility. The indexing correction remains incomplete because nearby text still references (x0,y0). Claims and experimental evidence are unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
